uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it moves rate expectations and the pound; the September figure also sets benefit uprating.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: This is the UK's reading for a September in which gasoline pushed annual inflation to 3.7% in the US and 3.1% in Canada. The release settles whether the same fuel-driven rise has reached UK consumer prices.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Warsh has withheld guidance, calling AI a shock to the economy, as gasoline lifted September inflation to 3.7%, above the Fed's target for 5.5 years. Most officials expect another hike by year-end, but the committee is split, and Trump has convened a panel on removing Governor Lisa Cook, one of its voters.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro-zone inflation is 3.8%, nearly double target, and officials called September's hike proportionate — but France's bond rout has widened its spread to Germany, Rehn says, while Moulin says no rescue is needed. The council weighs tightening against that strain a day after the 28 October deadline to nominate Isabel Schnabel's replacement.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and Japan's finance minister says the economy is shifting to a wage-driven inflation phase, the condition the Bank of Japan has set for tightening. The IMF has said the BOJ may need to move faster if inflation beats forecast; this meeting tests whether the board agrees.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: Greene, one of the committee's own members, said on the eve of this meeting's run-up that inflation risks are bigger than thought, a warning from inside the room rather than from markets. This decision settles how much weight the Bank of England gives that view when it sets the rate.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Gasoline lifted September inflation to 3.7%, and Fed officials are split over whether another hike is needed by year-end. Warsh has withheld guidance while calling AI a shock to the economy, and Trump has convened a panel on removing Lisa Cook, one of the governors who votes on the rate.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Putin has proposed a three-way summit with Trump and Xi that would seat no Ukrainian, and Trump says he is open to it. Zelenskyy is eyeing a meeting with the US and Russia on this summit's sidelines, so the gathering is where the argument over who sits at the table on Ukraine meets a fixed date.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro-zone inflation is 3.8%, nearly double target, after a September hike officials called proportionate. The complication is France: Rehn says its spread to Germany has widened 'somewhat' and Moulin that it needs no ECB help yet. So December weighs inflation against a member's rising borrowing costs.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: Greene, one of the Bank of England's rate-setters, said this week that inflation risks are bigger than thought, a warning from inside the committee rather than from markets. This meeting settles how many of Greene's colleagues have come round to that reading, and whether it is enough to move the rate.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Finance minister Katayama has said Japan is shifting to a wage-driven inflation phase, while yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago. The IMF has said the BOJ may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast; the board is weighing whether price rises are now home-grown or still imported through a weak yen.

fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on personal income and spending, carrying the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It moves rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis reports US PCE, settling how fast the prices households pay rose over the month and whether their spending kept pace with their income.

fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly estimate of US gross domestic product, first published about a month after each quarter ends and revised twice after. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed expectations move on it.
fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.recent: The release covers the third quarter, a stretch in which a Gulf war pushed oil near $110 and the IMF warned of a split outlook for 2026 growth. The figure settles how much of that shock reached US output and spending.
